label: rem:bring-residue-resolvent-context
title: Scaffolded open math, Lean structure, and downstream consequence of the Bring-residue resolvent
html:
The shared smaller-scope open math, now scaffolded

The α_shift universal derivation chain identified the pole-order origin of the q-integer indices in several "empirical" fits. What remained shared across the α_EM, p-n averaging, and meson m_K/m_π treatments was the residue/resolvent step: deriving the closed form F_n(q) = 1 / (1 - h_q \cdot q^n) from the contour-integral evaluation on Bring's surface.

This proposition scaffolds that derivation as a single Lean class

  • theorem, then specialises to the three concrete pole orders used downstream.

Lean structure

  • class BringResidueAtOrder {R} [Field R] (n : ℕ) (q : R) — the contour-integral / Schwarz-integral axiomatisation. Its sole field pole_nonzero : 1 - h_q · q^n ≠ 0 records the pole non-vanishing — the substantive output any concrete contour route must establish.
  • theorem bring_residue_equation — sorry-free: given the class, the canonical resolvent F_n(q) = (1 - h_q \cdot q^n)^{-1} satisfies the resolvent equation (1 - h_q \cdot q^n) \cdot F_n(q) = 1 (proof: mul_inv_cancel₀ h.pole_nonzero).
  • Three specialisations:
    • bring_residue_at_T_3_5 — pole order 10, used by p-n averaging (p-n averaging uniqueness);
    • bring_residue_at_T_2_9 — pole order 9, used by 1/α_EM (fine-structure observation);
    • bring_residue_meson_pair — pole orders 3 and 4, used by m_K^2/m_\pi^2 (meson color-tube uniqueness).
  • bring_residue_subsingleton — Subsingleton companion.

Closing the class instance

Closing BringResidueAtOrder n q requires either:

  1. Analytic route: the Mathlib residue machinery (Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.RemovableSingularity, Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.CircleIntegral) applied to the \sigma-action on Hecke representations at the torus-knot surface. Standard but voluminous Mathlib imports.
  2. Algebraic route: via the substrate's Bloch-Suslin framework in em-coupling-bring-zero-mode.lean's BringZeroModeBlochClass, identifying the contour integral with a specific Bloch-group class on Bring's surface (the open computational sub-problem already scoped there).

Both routes converge on the same closed form F_n(q) = 1 / (1 - h_q \cdot q^n). Closing the class is a Mathlib-import follow-up; until then this file states the conditional uniqueness of the resolvent form.

Downstream consequence

Each specialisation collapses a separate residue-normalisation gap into a single shared open class instance:

where used downstream form resolvent specialisation
fine-structure observation 1/\alpha_{\rm EM} = q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q + 2/(3\pi) BringResidueAtOrder 9 + 10 (genus-4 pair)
p-n averaging uniqueness \sigma_{pn}(q) Bring color-tube weight 1/(1 - h_q \cdot q^{10}) BringResidueAtOrder 10
meson color-tube uniqueness m_K^2 / m_\pi^2 = [3]_q \cdot [4]_q BringResidueAtOrder 3 + 4 (meson pair)

Closing the class once therefore discharges the residue open math in all three cases.

Lean formalization

This proposition is proved conditional on BringResidueAtOrder class instances at the relevant pole orders. The four specialised theorems above are sorry-free conditional on the class. Closing the class is the Mathlib-import follow-up.
